7.22.12.en: St. Macarius the Great * If anyone dedicates himself to God, if anyone does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please Him who has chosen him to be a soldier, if anyone withdraws from those who live a fleshly life and are immersed in worldly matters, if he seeks not the things which are on the earth but the things which are above (Col 3:1-2), such a man deserves to be called holy.

7.22.13.en: Origen * It is not considered an exaggeration to say (that a certain man is perfect or holy) if the man walks blamelessly and has not yet actually reached the end of his journey, but is still passing toward the end by a blameless way, free from deadly sins and at the same time purifying his unintentional sins by almsgiving, for the way in which we walk and by which we reach perfection is purified by pure prayer.

7.22.14.en: St. Augustine 4. Only-begotten (v. 22): The Wisdom of God is the only-begotten Son of God, who came down to us to raise us from the spirit of bondage to the spirit of adoption. For being the only-begotten Son, He joined us to Himself and made us sons of the Father by adoption, and this through the waters of Baptism, while He is the only-begotten Son by nature from eternity.

7.22.15.en: Now, though we are not worthy to be called servants of God, God calls us His sons, and how great is the difference between a son and a servant.

7.22.16.en: * As it happens that a man has great possessions, and has children and also servants, he gives the servants a kind of food different from the food he gives to his children born of him. For the children are the heirs of their father, they eat with him, because they resemble their fathers. So also Christ, the true Lord of the house, who created all things by Himself, bestows His favour on the wicked and the ungrateful. But the children whom He has begotten of Himself, to whom He has granted His grace, and in whom He is formed, these He provides - better than the others - with special delicacies and nourishment, food and drink. And as they go with Jesus their Father everywhere, He gives them Himself, as the Lord says: "He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him," and also: "he shall never see death" (Jn 6:56; 8:51). Those who possess the true inheritance have been born as sons of the heavenly Father, and dwell in their Father's house, as the Lord says: "And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever" (Jn 8:35).

7.22.17.en: St. Macarius the Great 5. Manifold (v. 22): He declares Himself in various ways.

7.22.18.en: * My God... Oh that I might know You, You who know me, that I might know You, O strength of my soul! Reveal Yourself to me, O Comforter of my soul!

7.22.19.en: Oh that I might behold You, O brightness of my eyes!

7.22.20.en: Make haste, O delight of my soul, that I may contemplate You, O joy of my heart!

7.22.21.en: Inspire me with Your love, for You are my life!

7.22.22.en: Shine upon me, for in You lies my true joy. In You is the sweetness of my rest. In You is my life. In You is the fulness of my glory!

7.22.23.en: St. Augustine 6. Subtle (v. 22): Immaterial and without substance, man cannot know His mysteries apart from His revelations. This is what moved the Son to become incarnate among us, to reveal Himself to our souls, and to offer Himself as a paradise to those who were deprived of it. Our Lord Jesus, the Word incarnate, came proclaiming on every occasion "I am..." the words of a loving God offering Himself to ignorant souls; had anyone else uttered them, he would have been a proud and arrogant man offering himself to human souls to usurp the place of God the Creator, who satisfies the souls of His creation.

7.22.24.en: * Support me, O eternal glory, my joy, reveal Yourself to me, O my God, that I may live!

7.22.26.en: The Lord Christ says: "My Father worketh hitherto, and I work" (Jn 5:17). He continues to work, for He is the beginning in our spiritual life, and He is the end. He begins with us working in us, walks with us as the Way, and in the end carries us to Himself, where we share His glory.

7.22.27.en: * Christ is the beginning of our virtue, He is the beginning of purity... Christ is the beginning of stewardship, for though He was rich, yet for our sakes He became poor (1 Cor 8:9). He is the beginning of patience, for when He was reviled, He reviled not again, and when He was struck, He did not strike. He is the beginning of humility, for He took upon Him the form of a servant, though in the greatness of His power He is equal to God the Father. In Him every virtue took its origin.

7.22.28.en: St. Ambrose 8. Piercing, going through all spirits, and passing into holy souls (vv. 22, 24, 27). 9. Pure (v. 22), untouched by defilement though present everywhere and working to sanctify sinners. 10. Clear (v. 22). 11. Sound (v. 22).

7.22.29.en: * Jesus, who destroys the defects within us, and brings down the most corrupt kingdoms of evil.

7.22.30.en: Origen 12. Loving what is good and beneficent (vv. 22, 23).

7.22.31.en: Since the Wisdom of God offers Himself as a treasure to us, enlightening our souls, satisfying our hearts, and bringing us into the riches of eternal glory, He is called the greatest good. He loves what is good, is beneficent to His creation, and desires to give Himself to every man, to carry him in Himself as the source of all good things, so that he lacks nothing at all.

7.22.32.en: * And now let us consider what the Gospels say in the light of the promises of good things. We must say that the good things proclaimed by the apostles in these Gospels are simply: Jesus. One of the good things they proclaim is the resurrection. But the resurrection is, in a certain way, Jesus, for He said: I am the resurrection.

7.22.33.en: * The heavenly things, even the heavenly Kingdom or Christ Himself, the King of the ages, are altogether "the kingdom of heaven" likened to "treasure hid in a field" (Mt 13:44).

7.22.34.en: What treasures? Compare the words "In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge" (Col 2:3). Those treasures are in Christ. From His fountain comes "the Spirit" with various kinds of gifts: to some gifts of wisdom, to some gifts of knowledge or gifts of faith, and to others any of the graces of God (1 Cor 12:8).

7.22.35.en: Origen * If there is anything good in me, its source is You; the good that is in me is Your goodness, O Good One, from You I have received it!

7.22.36.en: Who helps me to stand, if not You, O my God?!

7.22.37.en: And what makes me fall except my reliance on myself?!

7.22.38.en: I shall remain sunk in the mire unless You draw me up!

7.22.39.en: And I shall remain blind unless You open my eyes!

7.22.40.en: And I shall remain fallen, never rising, unless Your hands help me! I shall perish utterly unless Your providence guards me!

7.22.41.en: St. Augustine 13. Sharp (v. 22): that is, firm and just, along with His great love and infinite mercy. 14. Free (v. 23).

7.22.42.en: The divine Wisdom is free; death has no authority over Him, and He longs to see every man freed from every wrong thought and from every sin, so that eternal death and the devil may have no authority over him.

7.22.43.en: * Rightly is he called free who has authority to raise himself... and rightly is he called free who came down to save others.

7.22.44.en: St. Ambrose * Follow the heavenly Bridegroom, that you may stand firm against the invisible enemies, that you may wage war against principalities and powers (Eph 6:12), first drawing them away from yourself so that they have no share in you, and afterwards driving them away from those who fly to you seeking protection by your counsel. Cast them under your feet as their leader and defender. Renounce those arguments which are against faith in Christ.

7.22.45.en: Fight with the word of godliness against evil and wicked counsel. As the Apostle says: "Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God" (2 Cor 10:5). Put your trust, above all, in the arm of the great King, whose enemies fear and tremble at the mere sight of Him.

7.22.46.en: St. Basil the Great 15. Loving to man (v. 23).

7.22.47.en: The Wisdom of God, our Lord Jesus, who loves mankind, offered Himself as a sacrifice for their salvation, and He is gentle with us even in His anger and in His chastening of us.

7.22.48.en: * Remember the Shepherd who follows you and rescues you...

7.22.49.en: Remember the mercies of God, how He heals (like the good Samaritan) with oil and wine.

7.22.50.en: Do not despair of salvation, recalling to your memory what is recorded in the Holy Scripture, that he who falls shall rise, and the one who has gone astray shall return (Jer 8:4), and the wounded shall be healed, and the prey escapes (from the beast), and he who confesses his sin is not despised.

7.22.51.en: The Lord does not desire the death of the sinner, but rather that he should return and live (Ezek 18:32).

7.22.52.en: St. Basil the Great * The wrath of God is not a passion, otherwise man would have the right to despair, being unable to quench the flame of God's wrath kindled by man's own evil deeds. But God by nature is free from passion; even when He punishes and takes vengeance, He does not do so in fury, but out of concern for us, for in Him there is great tenderness and forgiveness. This urges us to have great and good courage, and to trust in the power of repentance...

7.22.53.en: Those who have sinned, even against Him, He does not desire to punish in vengeance for Himself, because no harm touches His divinity, but He does it for our benefit, and He prevents our deviation, which grows by our carelessness and indifference toward Him.

7.22.54.en: For just as he who remains outside, far from the light, does no harm to the light at all, but the greatest loss falls upon him for being in darkness, so he who is accustomed to despise the mighty power does not harm the power but harms himself with the greatest possible harm.

7.22.55.en: For this reason God threatens us with punishments, and even brings them upon us, not in vengeance for Himself but as a means of drawing us to Him.

7.22.56.en: * This is the tenderness of God, that He will not turn His face away from sincere repentance; for even if a man has been driven to the utmost limits of evil, when he returns to the way of virtue, God receives him and welcomes him, and does everything for him until He restores him to his first state.

7.22.57.en: For God works to the utmost limit of mercy, even if man does not show complete repentance; He does not overlook a small or trivial thing, but gives for this a great reward. This is evident from the words of the prophet Isaiah: "For the iniquity of his covetousness was I wroth, and smote him: I hid me, and was wroth, and he went on frowardly in the way of his heart. I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners" (Isa 57:17, 18).

7.22.58.en: And we shall cite another example, that of the most wicked of kings, who sinned under the influence of his wife, but as soon as he was sorry and put on sackcloth and condemned his faults, he gained for himself the mercies of God... For God said to Elijah: "Seest thou how Ahab humbleth himself before me? because he humbleth himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days" (cf. 1 Kgs 21:29).

7.22.59.en: St. John Chrysostom * God looks upon men, and cares for them in a special way, and leads all things by the ordering of His providence according to wisdom.

7.22.60.en: St. Macarius the Great 16. Steadfast in Himself, unchanging (vv. 23, 27).

7.22.61.en: Our Christ is the same yesterday, and today, and for ever (Heb 13:8), unchanging; He presents Himself as a firm rock on which His Church is built, so that the waves of the sea of this world cannot shatter her, nor can time make her grow old and weak.

7.22.62.en: * May you be built upon the rock if you do not want the flow of water or the winds or the rains to throw you down. If you want to arm yourselves against the temptations of this world, let your longing for the eternal Jerusalem build you up and strengthen your hearts.

7.22.63.en: * He emptied Himself, not because He changed from being the eternal Wisdom. For the eternal Wisdom will never change at all. Rather, without changing, He chose to become known to mankind in a humble form.

7.22.64.en: * It is good for me to hold me fast by God (Wis 7:27). For if I do not rest in Him, I do not rest in myself, but He is steadfast in Himself and makes all things new. And You are the Lord my God, for You exist and have no need of my goodness (Ps 16:2).

7.22.65.en: * Who is the likeness of Your Word, our Lord, who stands in Himself without growing old, and makes all things new.

7.22.66.en: St. Augustine * He who imitates Him is a rock.

7.22.67.en: Origen * The infinite God, while remaining unchanged, took flesh and fought death, freeing us from sufferings, freeing by His sufferings...! He Himself bound the strong man and spoiled his goods (Mt 12:29) - that is, He took us from him, we who had sunk into every evil, and made us vessels fit for the Master's use, as our free will became ready for every good work.

7.22.68.en: St. Basil the Great 17. Secure (v. 23). 18. Untroubled (v. 23).

7.22.69.en: Since the Wisdom of God is above all things, no harm will touch Him, and He gives security and tranquillity to whoever is joined to Him. He embraces His believers, as under His wings, shading them from the heat of trials and giving them the spirit of conquest and victory.

7.22.70.en: * We live under the shadow of the grace of Christ.

7.22.71.en: * No one boasted of his victory, or ascribed it to his personal courage, knowing that Jesus is the giver of victory, "let no man sharpen his tongue" (Sir 10:21). The Apostle understood this when he said: "yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me" (1 Cor 15:10).

7.22.72.en: May God guide me (after my winning the battle of life)... that I may not ascribe my victory to any merit of mine, but to His Cross.

7.22.74.en: * He is the One who was, and is, and ever remains... the true Son, steadfast, unchangeable, for He is God and the Son of the Almighty, all-powerful, yet He condescended for our salvation, to raise us up when we were cast down.

7.22.75.en: Lucifer 20. Overseeing all things and watching over everything (v. 23; 8:1), filling the world (Wis 8:1).

7.22.76.en: He is the searcher of hearts and reins, who knows all our thoughts and intentions, and comes to judge us according to our inner intentions, our words, and our conduct.

7.22.77.en: * Let us hate our sins for their own sake and love Him who comes to punish our sins. He is coming, whether we will or not.

7.22.78.en: St. Augustine 21. Going through all spirits (v. 23).

7.23.0.en: For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness. [24]

7.23.1.en: Faith in the Holy Trinity reveals the truth about God, that He is not an eternal, static being who moved only when He created the heavenly and earthly beings, but is an eternal movement of love existing within Himself among the Holy Trinity; it was never a latent power without action, but the act of love has existed from eternity.

7.23.2.en: This God, who is love at work, is always moving, and so He penetrates the human soul to purify it and sanctify it, and to make of it an icon of Himself, living and active.

7.23.3.en: The Wisdom of God is always present, for He says: "lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world" (Mt 28:20). And we shall also be with Him in the world to come.

7.23.4.en: Here we enjoy His presence with us and our fellowship with Him, and there we enjoy being in His embrace, delighting in the vision of Him face to face and having fellowship with Him in eternal glory.

7.23.5.en: * It is not enough that He says: "I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am" (cf. Jn 17:24), but He added: "be with me." For even the wretched man can be where God is, for wherever the wretched man is, God is also. But the blessed are alone with God, for it is by Him alone that they can be blessed. Was it not said of God: "If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there" (Ps 139:8)? Is not Christ the Wisdom of God who passes through every place because of her purity (Wis 7:24)? "The light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not" (Jn 1:3).

7.23.6.en: * If wisdom is God, the Creator of all things, as the divine authority and the truth testify (Wis 7:24-27), then the philosopher is a lover of God.

7.23.7.en: St. Augustine For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.

7.24.0.en: Therefore can no defiled thing fall into her. [25]

7.24.1.en: In his reply to Faustus (of the followers of Mani who regard matter, especially the body, as something unclean), St. Augustine affirms that the body in itself is not unclean because it is the work of the Good One. All things are pure to the pure; how much more does the Holy and Pure One look upon all creation as having nothing in it defiled or unclean in itself.

7.24.2.en: * The Apostle says: "Unto the pure all things are pure" (Titus 1:15). If this is true of men, who may be led to evil by a corrupt will, how much more is everything pure with respect to God, who remains always unchangeable and incapable of defilement...! It was said of divine Wisdom: "no defiled thing can fall into her, and she moves in every place because of her purity" (cf. Wis 7:24). It is extreme folly to find fault with human procreation (since they see uncleanness in the bodily relations between spouses), which was established by God, to whom all things are pure.

7.24.3.en: * Although all the things He established are in Him, yet he who sins does not defile Him, of whose wisdom it was said: "She touches all things by her purity, and nothing defiled assails her." For she urges us to believe that God is incorruptible and unchangeable, and thus He is uncorrupted.

7.25.0.en: St. Augustine For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness. [26]

7.25.1.en: The Lord Christ - the Wisdom of God - is called the brightness of the glory of the Father, because if God is light, there cannot be light without brightness, nor brightness without light. And there is no time separating the light from the brightness. For this reason, although the Wisdom of God is one with the Father in the same essence, and calls Himself: "I am the light of the world," He is also called "the brightness of the light." He shines upon souls, and they come into contact with the light and know it. "The only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him." He is the Word of the Father, speaking to us not through syllables of words but by the shining of Wisdom upon us.

7.25.2.en: * Are you seeking the Son without the Father? Give me light without the Father? Give me light without brightness. If there was a time when the Son was not, then the Father would be a dim light.

7.25.3.en: * If you can truly separate the brightness from the sun, then separate the Word from the Father.

7.25.4.en: * What the Father does, He does through the Son; by His wisdom and power He works, and does not act by anything outside Himself. He shows the Son what He sees, but in the Son Himself is shown what He does.

7.25.5.en: * If you see that there is no separation in the light, why do you seek a separation in the work (the work of the Holy Trinity)? Look at God, look at His Word, who does not dare... For the speaker does not utter syllables of words, but his speech is the shining of the brightness of Wisdom. What is said of Wisdom itself? "She is the brightness of the everlasting light." Observe the brightness of the sun in the sky, and it spreads its brightness over all the lands and all the seas although in its simplicity it is a sensible light. I speak of the sun; let us look at one small lamp with a feeble ray, which can be put out with one breath, and it spreads its light over everything near it, from the flame that is spread. You see an emanation from it and not a separation. Then understand, beloved brothers, that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are united together in themselves without separation. But this Trinity is the one God, and all the works of the one God are the works of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

7.25.6.en: * We read: "God is light, and in him is no darkness at all" (1 Jn 1:5), and also: "God, who commanded the light to shine ... in our hearts" (2 Cor 4:6). Also in the Old Testament He gave the name "the brightness of the everlasting light" (Wis 7:26) to the Wisdom of God, which certainly was not created, but by which all things were created. And of the light that proceeds from this Wisdom it was said: "For thou wilt light my candle: the Lord my God will enlighten my darkness" (Ps 18:28). In the same way, in the beginning, when darkness was upon the face of the deep, God said: "Let there be light: and there was light" (Gen 1:2), where He is the Light, the giver of light, and God Himself alone could do that.

7.25.7.en: St. Augustine * The prophet says: "In thy light shall we see light" (Ps 36:9). And also: "Wisdom is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the majesty of God, and the image of his goodness" (Wis 7:26). See what great names are proclaimed! "Brightness", because in the Son the glory of the Father shines clearly. "Unspotted mirror", for the Father is seen in the Son (Jn 12:45). "Image of his goodness", for it is not a body reflected on another, but all the power of the divinity is in the Son.

7.25.8.en: St. Ambrose * He who has illumination is greater than he who has intellect and knowledge. For the illuminated man has received more enlightenment of his mind than he who has knowledge only. As appears from his seeing visions within his soul, which cannot be open to doubt. But revelation is something higher than visions. For the great things of God and His mysteries are made known to the soul by revelation and inspiration.

7.25.9.en: * As our eyes behold the sun, so the illuminated behold the image of the soul, but few Christians attain to this illumination.

7.25.10.en: * Christians learn one new language, and all of them are refined by one wisdom, the Wisdom of God... And when Christians walk in this new creation, they receive new heavenly illumination and glories and mysteries which they obtain from seeing the visible things that they perceive with their senses.

7.25.11.en: St. Macarius the Great * Let us consider who our Savior is: the brightness of glory. The brightness of glory is begotten... our Savior is the Wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:24). And Wisdom is the brightness of the everlasting light (Wis 7:26). If the Savior is always begotten, therefore it is said: "before all the hills he begetteth me"... He is always begotten by the Father.

7.26.0.en: Origen And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new: and in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets. [27]

7.26.1.en: The Wisdom of Almighty God does not display His power before His creation, but in His love for it He works in it for its continual renewal. He does not change, and does not need to change, because His perfection is absolute and has no limits. He created mankind changeable, so that, on the one hand, He might give it freedom of will, with the right to grow continually, and with the power to bring its being down even to destruction. On the other hand, if mankind did not carry the possibility of change, it would remain in a state of stagnation, and life would have no flavour. So He renews it continually if it wills, without Himself changing.

7.26.2.en: * God is unchangeable, as it is written in the Psalms: "As a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same" (Ps 102:27), and in the Book of Wisdom: "remaining in herself, she maketh all things new" (Wis 7:27).

7.26.3.en: St. Augustine * Among our most important duties is the discernment of seasons and times, so that we may be able to practise virtue. The blessed Paul taught his disciple to observe the time, saying: "be instant in season, out of season" (2 Tim 4:2), so that when he knows the two times - the seasonable and the unseasonable - he may be able to do the things that suit the time and avoid what is unsuitable.

7.26.4.en: And so the God of all Himself gives everything in its time, as Solomon the wise says (Eccl 3:7), desiring thereby that the salvation of men should spread everywhere at the proper time.

7.26.5.en: And so "the wisdom of God" (1 Cor 1:24), our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, brought forth at the proper times, from holy souls, prophets and friends of God (Wis 7:27). Although many had offered prayers for Him (that He might come quickly to bring salvation), saying: "Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion!" (Ps 14:7), or as it is in the Song of Songs, on the lips of the bride saying: "O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother!" (Song 8:1), that is, would that You were like the sons of men, bearing the sufferings of mankind for us. In spite of all these prayers, the God of all, the Creator of seasons and times, who knows what is for our good better than we do, in the proper time, in the fulness of time, and not at some random time, declared as a skilful physician the way of our healing, sending His Son that we might obey Him, saying: "In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee" (Isa 49:8).

7.26.6.en: * God does not use one method of healing, but being rich He uses many ways for our salvation by His Word, who is not limited or restricted or hindered in the ways of healing which He sanctifies for us, but is rich, and able to shape Himself according to the needs and capacity of each soul.

7.26.7.en: He is the Word of God and His power and His wisdom, as Solomon testifies of Wisdom, saying: "And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new: and in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets" (Wis 7:27).

7.26.8.en: For those who have not yet reached the way of perfection, the Word is to them (1 Cor 3:2) like a flock that gives them milk. This is what Paul served them with when he says: "I have fed you with milk, and not with meat."

7.26.9.en: But for those who have advanced and passed the stage of perfect infancy, but are still weak as they seek perfection, for these also the Word is like food according to their capacity to bear. Paul served them with this also, when he said: "he that is weak eateth herbs" (Rom 14:2).

7.26.10.en: And for the man who begins to walk in the way of perfection, he no longer eats of the former things, but the Word is the bread, and the flesh the food, for it is written: "But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised" (Heb 5:14).

7.26.11.en: Rather, when the Word is sown, it does not bring forth equal fruit in all people, but there comes much and varied fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold (Mt 13:8), as the Savior, the sower of grace and giver of the Spirit, taught us.

7.26.12.en: And this is not a doubtful matter, nor in need of anyone to confirm it, but we can look at the field in which (the Lord) sows, for we find that the Word is clear and fruitful in the Church, not only by the virgins alone is the field adorned, nor by the monks alone, but also by those who are married in honourable marriage, and by the chastity of all...

7.26.13.en: The Lord has prepared many mansions with His Father (Jn 14:2), but although in the place of dwelling we find various degrees according to the progress of each one, yet we shall all be within the fortresses, kept within the same enclosure where the enemy (Satan) and all his company are driven outside.

7.26.14.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * What is impossible for the Wisdom of whom it is written: "being but one, she can do all things, and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new" (cf. Wis 7:27)? We read of Wisdom that she does not draw near but dwells. So you have the authority of Solomon, who teaches you of the omnipotence of Wisdom and her eternity, and also her goodness, for it is written: "But wisdom cannot be overcome by malice" (cf. Wis 7:30).

7.26.15.en: St. Ambrose * The Son delivered Himself, that being righteousness He might drive out the injustice that is in us. And Wisdom delivered herself, that she might drive out folly.

7.26.16.en: St. Jerome * The soul that returns to Him, seeking His mercy, and is in need of His protection, He brings to a blessed state, a state of freedom from the passions, and a state of continual steadfastness in every virtue by the renewing of the mind.

7.26.17.en: * Let no one imagine that his soul has been wholly enlightened all at once, completely. For there is still some measure of sin within, and man needs much toil and labour at the expense of the grace given to him.

7.27.0.en: St. Macarius the Great For God loveth none but him that dwelleth with wisdom. [28]

7.27.1.en: The Wisdom of God wants believers to be an icon of Him, characterized by the wisdom which they acquire through Him, so that they cleave to Him and He dwells in them. Therefore it is fitting for us to ask it from Him.

7.27.2.en: * This is the Paradise that never fails but overflows without limit, giving satisfaction as much as we receive, entreating all to receive Him, pleading: "Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him," and if he does not open to me, I knock once and again, that perhaps his heart will soften and open to me, because I love him!

7.27.3.en: He came incarnate, to restore to the soul its happiness and fill its sides, and remove anxiety from it.

7.27.4.en: O my poor soul, what do you seek?!

7.27.5.en: If you want wisdom, you find Jesus, the source of wisdom and its fountain, indeed He is Wisdom Himself!

7.28.0.en: St. Augustine For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it. [29]

7.28.1.en: * Now the form of the virtues is wonderful and amazing, especially the beauty of wisdom as all the Holy Scriptures tell us. For she is more beautiful than the sun, and when compared with the stars no group of them equals her. Night can overcome the light of a group of stars, but evil cannot overcome wisdom (Wis 7:29-30)... There is no fellowship between her and vice, but she is in union with the rest of the virtues without separation.

7.28.2.en: St. Ambrose * The joy of the soul of Your servant... Enter into my soul, O true Joy, that it may rejoice in You! Enter into it, O true Sweetness, pour upon it Your ray, O eternal Light, that it may know You and perceive You and love You...!

7.28.3.en: O Light that illuminates the soul, O radiant Truth, O true Brightness of illumination, You who lighten every man that cometh into the world. You came into the world, and the world loved You not!

7.28.4.en: My God... scatter the thick darkness that hangs over my soul, that it may see You when it perceives You, and know You when it receives You, and love You when it knows You.

7.28.5.en: St. Augustine For day succeeds night.

7.29.0.en: But wisdom shall not be overcome by evil. [30]

7.29.1.en: * Make haste, O Light, without whom I cannot see!

7.29.2.en: Support me, O eternal glory, my joy, reveal Yourself to me, O my God, that I may live!

7.29.4.en: Enter, O divine Wisdom, into my depths!

7.29.5.en: * Solomon preceded everyone and sought You that he might enjoy You!

7.29.6.en: He counted his throne and the sceptre of his kingdom as nothing!

7.29.7.en: Your dwelling satisfied his soul; he counted gold as a little sand.

7.29.8.en: And he saw silver as clay beside You.

7.29.9.en: You are his glory and his treasure and his riches!

7.29.10.en: * Teach me to follow his example, teach me how to seek You!

7.29.11.en: I know that You stand at the door and knock.

7.29.12.en: Let me open, and reign, and let no other reign over me but You.

7.29.13.en: * Enter, and by Your Holy Spirit continually renew my nature.

7.29.14.en: I see that You seek the beauty of my soul, which is the work of Your Spirit who calls.

7.29.15.en: How then can I waste my thought and my energies and my time in seeking the outward beauty of the body?

7.29.16.en: I possess You, O heavenly Physician and wonderful Remedy, and every sickness flees from my soul.

7.29.17.en: You are more precious than the health of my body!

7.29.18.en: * By what name shall I call You, O Wisdom of God?

7.29.19.en: You are the greatest Good, the source of all good things, You are the fountain of riches that never fails!

7.29.20.en: I possess You, and the doors of my heart are opened, that I may give my brothers of what You have given me.

7.29.21.en: I want everyone to enjoy You, so that all mankind may become storehouses of love that never empty!

7.29.22.en: * Grant me, with Solomon Your beloved, to call everyone to enjoy Wisdom.

7.29.23.en: Give me understanding and a word to speak of You, You whom no language can express!

7.29.24.en: * May all mankind possess You, so that there is no idle or negligent person among them.

7.29.25.en: May everyone work according to his gifts!

7.29.26.en: You shine upon the minds, and they perceive many mysteries, and knowledge grows, and learning increases, and everyone strives to search into everything in a spirit of humility.

7.29.27.en: They discover the mysteries of nature, the visible and the hidden!

7.29.28.en: * Allow me to speak of You, O Brightness of the divine light.

7.29.29.en: You are Spirit, wanting to give all mankind to live according to the Spirit and not the flesh!

7.29.30.en: You are the divine Mind, desiring to sanctify our minds by Yourself!

7.29.31.en: You are holy, longing that we may be sanctified by You!

7.29.32.en: You are the only-begotten Son of God, offering us adoption to the Father by Your Holy Spirit in the waters of Baptism.

7.29.33.en: You are gentle and merciful even in Your anger, chastening not that we may perish, but that we may live by You.

7.29.34.en: You are steadfast, entering into every soul and making of it a dwelling for Yourself.

7.29.35.en: You are mobile, working continually, that You may carry us to the bosom of Your Father.

7.29.36.en: You are pure, filling all things without defilement touching You!

7.29.37.en: You are clear, not withholding from us the revelation of Yourself.

7.29.38.en: You are perfect and sound, not divided; You fill heaven and earth, perfect in every place.

7.29.39.en: You are lover of what is good, for You are the greatest Good, desiring that those who believe in You become lovers of good even toward their opponents.

7.29.40.en: You are sharp and firm, for You do not tolerate evil, and do not accept corruption!

7.29.41.en: You are free; You gave Yourself to free us from the bondage of the devil, and from every sin.

7.29.42.en: You are the Beneficent One, Lover of mankind, raising up from us lovers of all mankind.

7.29.43.en: We shall not rest until all, if possible, find rest!

7.29.44.en: You are steadfast in Yourself, You will not change, You renew us that we may change and become better.

7.29.45.en: You are secure and untroubled, in You we enjoy security; our souls are filled with hope and rejoice, for in You we have a place in the bosom of Your Father.

7.29.46.en: You are Almighty, in You we can do all things, and we are not struck by weakness nor failure!

7.29.47.en: You are the Judge, watching even our thoughts and hidden intentions.

7.29.48.en: Not to lie in wait for our faults, but to sanctify us, reward us, and glorify us!

7.29.49.en: You go through all spirits, for You are their life; without You they have no life!

7.29.50.en: You are present in every place; wherever we are, we find a living witness to You.

7.29.51.en: Behold, nature cries out bearing witness to You.

7.29.52.en: Behold, history proclaims Your continual care.

7.29.53.en: Behold, events confirm that You are the Ruler of all.

7.29.54.en: Behold, my depths declare to me that I have no refuge but You.

7.29.55.en: * Finally, what do I ask of You, O eternal Light.

7.29.56.en: That I may possess You, so that darkness does not creep into me.

7.29.57.en: All the lights of the world will be extinguished one day, but Your light is eternal.

7.29.58.en: You are my light and my glory, You are my treasure and my riches, You are my joy and my delight, You are my satisfaction and my glory, You are all to me!
